convoLines.text: "I can't reach this properly. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Nina is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sleep's gone strange. I sit apart to eat at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"My wound needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"I dreamed Nina was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Avery digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+868 kcal to the pantry.)
"I keep turning over the last thing Nina said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Avery grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Avery is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some Serviceberry today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that plant lesson."
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "The whole fire was arguing about The Anaconda Empress last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Ugly Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"I listen to everyone and nod. It's a strategy. Probably."
"Go on, then. I'll be thinking good thoughts at you."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Avery sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"All right —" Avery starts to stand, then sinks back down. "Maybe not today. The fire's got me."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Have you heard what they're calling The Anaconda Empress? Javier is pushing 'Big-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Avery is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"My part? I do push-ups at dawn and stay neutral until there's a winner."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You told me your trade. I've been watching your hands since — they know things."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Ghost Pipe — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I dreamed Ruth was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"My wound needs a second pair of hands. Will you help me clean it?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Ruth owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I keep turning over the last thing Ruth said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"Love that for us — I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You saw it too, right? Pantry Raid. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Avery nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration."
"trapping. Sounds small. But small useful things stack — and one day you look up and you're the person everyone asks. That's how it happens."
"Still on the most useful thing you've learned."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "They took Sydir — Pantry Raid, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I count portions out loud before eating. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Sydir nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said the most useful thing you learned is being hungry and going anyway. Still the lesson?"
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff. Life's funny that way."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Yeah? What's up?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took me. Hardened Who Ate It? — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Hey — I found some Elderberry today. You were right, it was right where you said."
Sydir has an edge today — something curdled.
"a cellar full of jars — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that plant lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." Someone has to be the memory of this place. I've volunteered.
"A hundred years from now someone should know we were here and what it cost."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Kwaku nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it? That's my read."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing."

"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The whole fire was arguing about Sunbasker last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Ugly Bastard' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"Yeah? What's up? Famous last words."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "That's where we are."
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
"Still on each other. ...sorry."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet. Doesn't matter now."
Mateo has an edge today — something curdled.
"This one — Water Lily. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Cattail. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I already told you what happened." Mateo crosses their arms. "Asking again doesn't change it."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Hah. Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
"Have you heard what they're calling Sunbasker? Sydir is pushing 'The Ugly Bastard'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Names are for when it's dead or known. Right now it's neither, so I hum one note, over and over, when the dark comes instead."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"About grief — yeah, we never did get back to that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never did finish talking about grief — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'Hah. Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there.'"
"This one — Prickly Pear. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Senegal Date Palm. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
Quiet for a long time. Then, barely audible: "I took 1× Stone. I won't do it again."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"You want to know about that? Okay." I want one day where I laugh until it hurts and it's not from nerves.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"I'm collecting jokes like firewood. We'll need them when it's dark."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on wanting to laugh again, properly."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Sydir nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"The pantry run — I haven't stopped thinking about it."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Meet me at the south slope below the meadow and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"a ridge with a view for miles — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want the truth? I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to preserve who they were. The truth felt small. The lie felt like someone worth keeping around. Happy now?"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
"Still on that foraging help."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lines: d20: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Klaus Patterson is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d20: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d20: 🕯️ Klaus Patterson is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d20: What Klaus kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.

d20: 🌲 Something still paces the treeline beyond the walls — Headlight Harry — waiting for a dead Klaus. It doesn't come in. The walls end the argument. (Haven is sanctuary. It'll still be out there when the new bearer leaves.)
d20: "Klaus's gone." Javier looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Klaus." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d20: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Catalina blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d20: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d20: 📖 LEARNED: Patient Aim (Level 1). One shot. You don't take the shot unless it's the shot.
d20: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Weather (Level 1). Red sky at night, shepherd's delight. Red sky at morning, shepherd's warning. It works.
d20: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d20: 📖 LEARNED: Wire Snares (Level 1). A loop of wire on a game trail. Simple, effective, ancient. Check at dawn.
d20: 📖 LEARNED: Reading the Water (Level 1). You know where fish hold: seams, eddies, shade lines. The water stops being a surface and starts being a map.
d20: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d20: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Klaus Patterson, 20 days. The mantle passes to Catalina Reyes.
d20: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Catalina Reyes, 38 — a fishing guide. Her hands know different work now: Bloodhound.
d20: The village's quarrel was with Klaus — and Klaus is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d20: At the grave, Javier, Avery, Ruth speak for Catalina — "Klaus trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d20: The fire knew Catalina before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.
